gaps.concept: PTH stimulates osteoblast RANKL expression, indirectly activating osteoclasts and increasing bone resorption.
gaps.why_tested: Explains bone loss in a patient with elevated PTH despite osteoclasts lacking a direct PTH response.

gaps.concept: PTH increases distal renal calcium reabsorption and decreases proximal phosphate reabsorption.
gaps.why_tested: Predicts calcium and phosphate changes when a question asks where PTH acts in the nephron.

gaps.concept: PTH stimulates renal 1α-hydroxylase; calcitriol then increases intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption.
gaps.why_tested: Connects elevated PTH to calcitriol production and distinguishes direct renal effects from indirect intestinal effects.

gaps.concept: Primary hyperparathyroidism may present as incidental hypercalcemia with an inappropriately normal, unsuppressed PTH level.
gaps.why_tested: An asymptomatic patient has high calcium and a PTH result within the laboratory reference range.

gaps.concept: A parathyroid adenoma is usually a single encapsulated chief-cell lesion with a rim of compressed normal gland; hyperplasia involves multiple glands.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes adenoma from multigland hyperplasia on histology or operative findings.

gaps.concept: MEN1 involves a menin tumor-suppressor defect; MEN2A involves activating RET mutations and can cause multigland parathyroid hyperplasia.
gaps.why_tested: A familial endocrine-tumor vignette asks which genetic syndrome explains hyperparathyroidism.

gaps.concept: Inferior parathyroids arise from the third pharyngeal pouch and descend with the thymus; superior parathyroids arise from the fourth pouch.
gaps.why_tested: Tests embryologic origin or an ectopic inferior parathyroid in the thymus or mediastinum.

gaps.concept: DiGeorge-associated hypoparathyroidism results from a 22q11.2 deletion that disrupts pharyngeal-pouch development.
gaps.why_tested: An infant with hypocalcemic tetany and thymic hypoplasia prompts identification of the developmental defect.

gaps.concept: Pseudohypoparathyroidism causes hyperphosphatemia because renal tubules resist PTH-mediated phosphate excretion.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes PTH resistance from vitamin D deficiency in a patient with hypocalcemia and elevated PTH.

gaps.concept: Maternal GNAS defects impair Gsα–cAMP signaling and may also cause resistance to TSH and other peptide hormones.
gaps.why_tested: Albright hereditary osteodystrophy appears with elevated PTH and TSH despite intact glands.

gaps.concept: Severe hypomagnesemia suppresses PTH secretion and causes peripheral PTH resistance, producing hypocalcemia.
gaps.why_tested: Hypocalcemia persists despite calcium replacement in a patient with marked magnesium depletion.

gaps.concept: Vitamin D deficiency typically causes low 25-hydroxyvitamin D, low phosphate, and elevated alkaline phosphatase.
gaps.why_tested: Differentiates nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism from CKD-associated phosphate retention.

gaps.concept: CKD-associated renal osteodystrophy may produce vertebral endplate sclerosis called a rugger-jersey spine.
gaps.why_tested: A spine radiograph accompanies elevated PTH and phosphate in a patient with longstanding CKD.

gaps.concept: Hypocalcemia causes perioral paresthesias, tetany, and Chvostek or Trousseau signs.
gaps.why_tested: A neuromuscular-excitability vignette asks for the underlying electrolyte disorder.

gaps.concept: Hypocalcemia prolongs the QT interval; hypercalcemia shortens it.
gaps.why_tested: An ECG finding is used to identify the direction of a calcium disturbance.

gaps.concept: Low albumin lowers total calcium while ionized calcium can remain normal.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with hypoalbuminemia has low measured total calcium without symptoms of true hypocalcemia.

gaps.concept: Alkalosis increases calcium binding to albumin, lowering ionized calcium despite normal total calcium.
gaps.why_tested: Hyperventilation triggers paresthesias or carpopedal spasm with a normal total calcium result.

gaps.concept: Granulomatous macrophages can produce unregulated 1α-hydroxylase, raising calcitriol and calcium while suppressing PTH.
gaps.why_tested: Sarcoidosis or tuberculosis accompanies hypercalcemia and elevated 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D.

gaps.concept: PTHrP-mediated hypercalcemia usually lowers phosphate; calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia tends to raise phosphate.
gaps.why_tested: Phosphate and vitamin D results distinguish mechanisms of malignancy-associated hypercalcemia.

gaps.concept: Vitamin D toxicity raises both calcium and phosphate and suppresses PTH.
gaps.why_tested: Supplement exposure and hyperphosphatemia distinguish vitamin D excess from primary hyperparathyroidism.

gaps.concept: Calcium-alkali syndrome combines excessive calcium and absorbable alkali intake with hypercalcemia, metabolic alkalosis, and kidney injury.
gaps.why_tested: A patient taking large amounts of calcium carbonate has this characteristic laboratory triad.

gaps.concept: Lithium shifts the calcium-sensing receptor set point, permitting PTH secretion despite elevated calcium.
gaps.why_tested: Chronic lithium use accompanies hypercalcemia with an unsuppressed PTH level.

gaps.concept: Thiazides increase distal tubular calcium reabsorption and reduce urinary calcium excretion.
gaps.why_tested: A medication history explains hypercalcemia or alters interpretation of urinary calcium testing.

gaps.concept: Marked hypercalcemia impairs renal concentrating ability, causing polyuria, dehydration, and worsening hypercalcemia.
gaps.why_tested: Polyuria and volume depletion accompany a high calcium level without primary diabetes insipidus.

gaps.concept: Cinacalcet activates the parathyroid calcium-sensing receptor, reducing PTH secretion.
gaps.why_tested: A pharmacology question asks how a drug lowers calcium in PTH-driven hypercalcemia.

gaps.concept: Denosumab blocks RANKL, preventing osteoclast formation; hypocalcemia is a possible adverse effect.
gaps.why_tested: The stem asks for the target or electrolyte effect of an antiresorptive treatment.

gaps.concept: Bisphosphonates inhibit osteoclast-mediated bone resorption; osteonecrosis of the jaw is a recognized adverse effect.
gaps.why_tested: An antiresorptive treatment is linked to its mechanism or a characteristic complication.

gaps.concept: Symptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism is treated definitively with parathyroidectomy.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with PTH-driven hypercalcemia and kidney stones requires selection of definitive treatment.

gaps.concept: Severe symptomatic hypocalcemia is treated initially with intravenous calcium.
gaps.why_tested: Tetany, seizure, or arrhythmia from hypocalcemia prompts a first-line treatment choice.

gaps.concept: Hungry bone syndrome follows abrupt PTH reduction after parathyroidectomy as remineralizing bone takes up calcium, phosphate, and magnesium.
gaps.why_tested: Prolonged postoperative hypocalcemia with low phosphate must be distinguished from gland injury.
